title: Average Waiting Time
statement: A restaurant has one chef. Given an array of customer arrivals and preparation times, calculate the average waiting time for all customers. Customers wait until the chef finishes their order, and the chef works on one order at a time in the order they were given. Results within 0.00001 of the actual answer are acceptable.
constraints: Customers arrive in increasing order and have positive preparation times.
Waiting time runs from arrival through completion; return the average.
hints: Each order starts at the later of its arrival and the previous completion.
Track the chef’s finish time and add finish-arrival for each customer.
Update finish=max(finish,arrival)+duration, accumulate its wait, then divide by customer count.
Single-chef input order fixes every start once the prior finish is known, so the simulation is exact.
editorial: Single-chef input order fixes every start once the prior finish is known, so the simulation is exact.

tests.explanation: Completion times three, eight, and eleven give waits two, six, and seven, averaging five.
The chef may idle before arrivals; the average wait is 3.25.
